question: An 18-year-old man presents to his primary care provider before leaving for college. He has no complaints. His past medical history is significant for asthma, acne vulgaris, and infectious mononucleosis at age 16. His home medications include doxycycline and albuterol as needed. His family history is significant for colon cancer in his father at age 50, his paternal grandfather at age 55, and an uncle at age 45. His father underwent testing for mutations in the APC gene, which were negative. There is no family history of dental abnormalities or other malignancy. The patient denies any recent weight loss, abdominal pain, hematochezia, melena, or other changes in the appearance of his stools. This patient should be screened for colorectal cancer (CRC) under which of the following protocols?

options.opa: Colonoscopy every 1-2 years beginning at age 25
options.opb: Colonoscopy every 5 years beginning at age 40
options.opc: Colonoscopy every 10 years beginning at age 40
options.opd: Colonoscopy every 10 years beginning at age 50

analysis: Given the significant family history of colon cancer in close relatives at relatively young ages, along with the patient's personal history of asthma and acne vulgaris, it would be prudent to consider earlier screening for colorectal cancer. The presence of a family history of colon cancer is a major risk factor for developing the disease. Therefore, the patient should be screened more frequently and at an earlier age than average-risk individuals.
